$comment: The code that reads design/session-distill/ledger.json, as data (plan WP-13, F36). `migrate-ledger.py --check` compares it with a discovery over the tracked code files (.py .js .mjs .cjs .sh .toml) in three layers: `text` (the file names ledger.json), `ast` (a Python scope assembles the path from `session-distill` and `ledger.json`, in one statement or several) and `argument` (a line of a file with one of the pattern's suffixes matches one of `argument_patterns`, the way a workflow script handed the ledger's rows names them). A file found by any layer is a reader or a mention, and the one this list lacks fails by path. `path_built` is `literal` (the text layer must find it) or `components` (the AST layer must find it) when the file builds the path itself, `imported` when it receives the module that does, and `argument` when it receives the rows: an argument reader carries a `witness` pattern that must still match its source. `reads` are the schema 1 field names the reader depends on; an entry marked `via` ledger_compat reads the projection, not the entry. `mentions_only` are files that name the ledger in prose or a comment and read nothing; each carries its reason, and an entry whose file stops naming the ledger fails as stale.
limits: A reader that gets the ledger's rows through a channel no layer names (a pipe from another program, a path read from configuration, a file copied under another name) is invisible to all three layers.

The AST layer reads Python only, and combines string constants within one module, function or class scope; a path whose pieces sit in different scopes, or are joined from names or imported constants, is found only when the text layer sees `ledger.json` as a literal.

An argument reader is found by `argument_patterns`, each limited to the suffixes whose scripts take arguments that way (a Python `args.ledger` is an argument parser, and the decision ledger has one); a new reader that names the rows differently is not found until a pattern is added.
Only code files are searched. Markdown, JSON and the design records are not, so a runbook that tells a person to open the ledger is not a reader here.
A mention in a comment, a docstring or a string of prose is reported like a reader and has to be listed under `mentions_only`.

readers.via: direct, through runlib/ledger.py's check_command; it is where the checkout's path lives
the rows `args.ledger` carries, which the runbook (guides/session-distill-workflow.md, step 5) builds from the ledger's entries until the cutover
direct, through runlib/ledger.py's ledger_path: `--ledger` when given, else the state root's own
direct, until the cutover replaces its body with runlib/ledger.py
direct; author-side, and it names the checkout's ledger itself since shipped code may not
direct, over the path its caller names (`ledger_path`/`--ledger`); the module itself builds none

mentions_only.reason: the umbrella passes the checkout's ledger to the two suites that need it (`gates/check-ledger.py`, `lifecycle_intake.py --checkout-ledger`); it reads no field of the ledger itself, and the path lives here because shipped code may not name it (WP-24)
the Session distill preset's mission names the file in prose; no code of the launcher reads it
a docstring names the ledger's shape; the module validates learning records and reads no ledger
names its own per-run supervisor ledger (run_dir/supervisor/ledger.json), a different file; reads nothing of design/session-distill/ledger.json
